critical_changes: Genuine-painting control (Sec 5.3, App D, Sec 6). Appendix D says the control uses 'two works per painter' per pseudo-scene, but painter_specificity_review_v1.real_controls draws the two pseudo-repeats with replacement, so one painting can fill both repeats. That duplicate reintroduces within-painter variance into the cross-repeat product. Recompute with distinct works: my rerun gives means of 0.111/0.252/0.373 instead of 0.234/0.753/0.731. Also account for the larger half-collection and class-specific target noise. Then revise or remove 'FLUX.2 Max's 0.801 is close to the content-sampled genuine level; the other configurations are not' and adjust the Sec 6 recommendation.

Qualify the headline 'three configurations have larger errors than a generator that makes no painter distinctions' (Abstract, Sec 1 bullet 3, Sec 5.3). (a) It holds only in the 31 features: in CLIP five of six D estimates exceed 1, with GPT Image 1 lowest at 0.847; in CSD none do. (b) D vs 1 is a descriptive comparison outside the prespecified 21-comparison family (protocol v2). (c) GPT Image 1's exceedance does not survive a 6-way Bonferroni adjustment ([0.935, 2.210]); Flare's and Sunburst's do.

Narrow the feature-family contribution (Sec 1 bullet 5, Sec 5.5, Table 6). Texture minus spatial is -2.9 points [-14.1, +10.2] in a paired scene bootstrap, with texture below spatial in only about 68% of resamples; texture minus color is below zero in about 99.6%. Report paired family-difference intervals and state only what is supported: texture is less shared than color; the texture/spatial ordering is unresolved; orderings differ by configuration.
minor_changes: Sec 5.2, last sentence: qualify 'for a faithful imitator alike'. The faithful CSD share for GPT Image 2 is 48.3%, its observed share is 54.2% [47.4, 59.3], and Cezanne's per-painter CSD shares go as low as 34.6%.
Table 11 caption: repeat noise is half the squared difference between the repeats' centered contrasts, relative to H.
App D: 'GPT Image 2's differences are about twice the reference size' should say twice in squared size (1.49 times in norm, as in Sec 5.3).
App C, exchangeable null: 1/4 is E[N]/(E[N]+E[B]), not the expected shared fraction.

Report the protocol-prescribed nominal and paired-bootstrap intervals for the 15 pairwise D differences, labelled unadjusted. The bootstrap excludes zero for 8/15 pairs, nominal t for 6/15, simultaneous for 2/15.
Sec 5.6: separate the cropped-only and refit results. Cropped only: Flare-FLUX is the only resolved pair. Refit: GPT Image 1-FLUX and Flare-FLUX are resolved.
Report how bootstrap draws with non-positive denominators were handled (family means: 32 spatial and 4 texture draws out of 5,000).
State that Eq. 4 uses the unnormalized prototype (mean of reference cosines) while recognition uses unit prototypes. Add that normalized-prototype gains change the shares by at most 0.5 points.
Note that correcting the finite-sample bias of H also changes Q, D, B/H and both benchmarks, not only beta.
Add scene intervals or stability frequencies for the CLIP and CSD D values in Table 4.
Repeat dependence: note that a shared repeat component would also inflate N and B (the shared fraction), not only D.
Sec 1 bullet 3: rephrase 'only FLUX.2 Max is below that level in 94.2%...' so that it does not read as if no other configuration is ever below 1.

App C 'Intervals': clarify 'describe these 14 scenes rather than fresh requests'. Between-scene standard errors are conservative for fixed scenes; the intervals do not generalize because the scenes are authored.
Commit to releasing the generated images with the camera-ready version (subject to service terms) so the features can be re-extracted.
Clarity: reduce the density of numbers in the prose (abstract, Sec 5.1, Sec 5.3) and add a short reading guide mapping each quantity to the question it answers.
App H: the claim check matches each literal anywhere in the text. Anchor claims to their sentences, and compute caption literals such as the Table 14 shares instead of hard-coding them.
factual_errors: App D 'Genuine-painting controls' describes 'two works per painter for each of 14 pseudo-scenes', but the implementation samples with replacement, so the same work can appear as both repeats. The reported means 0.234/0.753/0.731 depend on this: with distinct works they are 0.111/0.252/0.373. The Sec 5.3 statement that FLUX.2 Max's 0.801 is close to the content-sampled genuine level is therefore not supported.
Table 11 caption defines repeat noise as the squared difference between repeats relative to H. The printed values are half the squared difference.
App D says GPT Image 2's differences are 'about twice the reference size', which conflicts with Sec 5.3 ('1.49 times the reference size in norm'). Q = 2.223 is a squared size.
